sons.seo: Sleep Sounds With No Ads: Rain Sounds, Waves and Forests
sons.desc: Sleep sounds with no ads: rain, ocean waves, forest streams, flutes and soft drones on a 5 to 60 minute timer. A gentler alternative to white noise, offline.
sons.h1: Sleep sounds with no ads: rain sounds, ocean waves, flutes and soft drones
sons.lead: MeditaDream is a free sleep sounds app, made for winding down at the end of the day. Its thirteen sounds come in three families, from rain and ocean waves to flutes and soft drones. Its free nature sounds for sleep are real recordings, made in forests, beside a Highland stream and by the ocean. You can play any of them on its own, with a timer that fades out gently. During a guided meditation, you can also play one softly under the voice. Like everything in the app, the sounds come with no subscription, no ads and no account.

sections.h2: Rain sounds for sleep and other nature sounds
p: The nature family brings together five real recordings. After Rain mixes falling rain with rainforest sounds, for sleep or for a quiet break. The Ocean Waves sound is the ocean itself, wave after wave. Highland Stream carries the steady flow of a stream in the Scottish Highlands.

Two forests complete the family. Woodland was recorded in a forest in the Netherlands, alive with birds. Northwoods takes you to a vast northern forest full of birdsong. Both are gentle forest sounds for sleep, lively without being loud. For rain, start with After Rain, then try Ocean Waves on another evening.

sections.h2: Free meditation music for sleep: flutes, a singing bowl and throat singing
p: The second family, instruments and voices, is the closest thing to relaxation music in the app. Resonance is a singing bowl that sounds once every four minutes, like a slow singing bowl meditation. Chinese Flute features the dizi, a traditional Chinese flute, for soft meditation music with a melody. Xiao brings back the xiao flute every five minutes. This end-blown flute is a cousin of the Japanese shakuhachi, the flute of zen meditation music.

Khoomei is overtone throat singing, in which a single voice produces two notes at once. For many listeners, it is spiritual meditation music. Fairy Tale plays classic fairy-tale themes, a gentle kind of relaxing sleep music. Choose this family when silence feels too empty but words feel like too much. On anxious evenings, it can serve as relaxation music for anxiety, soft and wordless. These sounds can also keep you company while you read, stretch or simply rest.

sections.h2: Soundscapes, drones and binaural beats
p: The third family is the most minimal. Nebula is a soft, spacious soundscape with a cosmic feel. Monolith is a deep drone built on low subharmonics, for when you want a sound to sink into. If you usually play deep sleep music, start with Monolith.

Theta uses binaural beats. Each ear hears a slightly different tone, and the 4 Hz gap between them falls in the theta range. That is why Theta needs headphones: each ear must hear its own tone. Some people look for binaural beats for sleep, others for astral projection binaural beats. Both often use this theta range, linked to drowsiness. Nothing here promises a particular effect, so take Theta simply as a sound, and keep it if you like it.

sections.h2: A sleep sounds timer that fades out on its own
p: Timed Ambience plays a single sound, with no voice, for the length of time you pick: from 5 minutes to an hour. At the end, the sound fades out over six seconds, then stops. Locking the screen does not interrupt it, so you can put your phone down and close your eyes.

The timer is handy beyond bedtime too. Try ocean waves for relaxation during a break, or half an hour of Highland Stream while you read. On waking, Chinese Flute makes gentle morning meditation music.

sections.h2: Looking for white noise?
p: MeditaDream has no synthetic white noise. Instead, it offers real recordings of rain, relaxing ocean sounds and running water: After Rain, Ocean Waves and Highland Stream. A recording keeps the small irregularities of a real place, while white noise sounds the same from one moment to the next.
If you would rather have a sound without water, Nebula is a soft cosmic soundscape. If you usually listen to white noise at night, these are good places to start.

sections.h2: How to use sleep sounds at bedtime
p: At night, nothing should interrupt you: just sleep sounds, no ads, no login screen. MeditaDream has neither ads nor accounts, so the sound simply plays. A few habits can make it even more pleasant:
ul: Keep the volume low: soothing sounds for sleep work best when you barely hear them. The same goes for deep sleep meditation music, such as Resonance or Xiao.
Use headphones for Theta. The other sounds play well through your phone's speaker.
Match the timer to the time you need to drift off, such as 30 minutes of ocean sounds for sleep.
Choose a continuous sound, such as Highland Stream, if you prefer nothing to change. Resonance and Xiao come back at intervals, like zen music for sleep.
Give one sound a few evenings before you switch to another.

faq: Is this sleep sounds app really free?
Yes, completely: these free calming sounds for sleep come with no subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases and no account. The app is available on the App Store and Google Play.
Do I need headphones?
Only for Theta, because its binaural beats need each ear to hear its own tone. All the other sounds work through the phone's speaker.
Can I hear these sounds during a meditation?

Yes. During a guided meditation, tap “Background sound” in the player to play one softly under the voice. Add After Rain to a breathing session for a simple rain sounds meditation. Each immersive world also has its own ambience, and Timed Ambience plays a sound on its own.
What are the best sleep sounds to try first?

If you like rain sounds for sleep, start with After Rain. It also comes closest to jungle sounds for sleep, with its tropical forest. If you prefer sleep music, flute is a gentle place to start. Try Chinese Flute first, then Fairy Tale, and compare them over a few evenings.
Can I play sleep sounds offline?
Yes. These thirteen sounds come inside the app, so they play with no connection, even in airplane mode. That also makes it a handy rain sounds app for trips and nights away.
What are good calming sounds for anxiety?

Many people find steady sounds easiest, such as Highland Stream or Ocean Waves, played low on the timer. Others prefer Nebula, a soft soundscape with no water. These sounds offer a moment of rest. If anxiety weighs on you, talk to a professional.
Is MeditaDream a meditation music app?

Not exactly: it has no playlists and no songs. Its thirteen sounds include soft instruments, such as two flutes, a singing bowl and the orchestral themes of Fairy Tale. You can play one on its own with the timer, or softly under a guided meditation.

gratitude.seo: Free Gratitude Journal App with Guided Gratitude Meditations
gratitude.desc: A free gratitude journal app with eleven sections, plus guided gratitude meditations. No subscription, no ads, no account, works offline.
gratitude.h1: A free gratitude journal app: notice the good, one line at a time
gratitude.lead: A gratitude journal is a small ritual: each day, you write down a few things you are grateful for. In MeditaDream, the Gratitude & Growth journal gives this ritual a home, with eleven sections and guided gratitude meditations to go with it. Everything you write stays on your phone. It is a gratitude app free of subscriptions, ads and accounts.

sections.h2: What is a gratitude journal?
p: A gratitude journal, or gratitude diary, is a notebook for the good things in your life, big or small. You might note a kind word, a good meal or a quiet moment in the sun. Writing them down is a way to slow down and really notice them.

There is nothing to perform and nothing to prove. The journal simply invites you to look at your day from a slightly different angle, and to keep a trace of what went well. Some days, it is a short gratitude list. On a hard day, one small thing is enough.
Gratitude does not mean pretending that everything is fine. It sits next to the rest of your day, without erasing it.

sections.h2: How to start a gratitude journal, simply
p: The simplest method is often the one you will keep. There is no right length and no perfect moment, only a rhythm that suits you. If you wonder what to write in a gratitude journal, here are a few ideas:
ul: Write one to three things a day. A single line is enough.
Be specific: name the exact moment, like a message from a friend or the smell of rain.
Pick a regular time, such as bedtime or your morning coffee.
Include yourself now and then: something you did well also counts.
Think of people too, and what they brought to your day.
Keep it private. It is easier to be honest when no one else will read it.
If you miss a day, simply start again the next one.

sections.h2: Inside the Gratitude & Growth journal
p: The Gratitude & Growth journal is made for what you are grateful for, and for where you want to grow. Daily Gratitude is the natural place to start: think of it as your daily gratitude journal.

Its sections work like journal prompts for gratitude, which makes it a guided gratitude journal. You do not need to use them all, though. Daily Gratitude alone can carry the habit for a long time, and the others wait for the days when you want to explore further.

Some sections stay close to gratitude itself, such as Self Gratitude or Relationship Gratitude. Others turn toward growth, like Emotional Growth or Growth Tracker. Self Discovery and Forgiveness Practice go deeper, for evenings when you have more time. Here are all eleven:
ul: Daily Gratitude
Self Gratitude
Relationship Gratitude
Emotional Growth
Evolution, Confidence & Self-Worth
Spiritual Growth
Micro Victories
Growth Tracker
Gratitude through Life
Self Discovery
Forgiveness Practice

sections.h2: Gratitude meditation, from the body to the people who matter
p: Daily Gratitude is also the name of a 14-minute guided session. It begins in the body, with simple thanks for your legs, your sense of taste and your breath. Played after waking, it makes a gentle morning gratitude meditation.

Precise Gratitude takes only 3 minutes: you pick one particular thing you truly value and rest your whole attention on it. For a longer gratitude meditation, try Gratitude to Your Guides, which lasts 23 minutes. It is a chance to thank, in turn, the people who have counted in your life, even those you never met. A Buddhist gratitude meditation often follows the same path, thanking the strangers whose work brought you your food. Two more sessions, on self-love and compassion, complete the selection.

sections.h2: A gratitude journal app that stays on your phone
p: Your journal is personal. Unlike an online gratitude journal, everything you write stays on your phone, and there is no account to create. With no ads and no subscription, nothing interrupts the moment you take for yourself.
The guided meditations download once, then play offline. Alongside Gratitude & Growth, the app includes four other journals, such as the Dream Journal and the Emotional Journal.

sections.h2: Gratitude before bed: a simple evening ritual
p: If you want an evening gratitude practice, pair the journal with a short gratitude meditation. It only takes a few minutes:
ul: Listen to Precise Gratitude, which lasts 3 minutes.
In the journal, go to Daily Gratitude and write one line.
Read it back once, slowly, before you put your phone away.
On busy evenings, keep only the first step: three minutes is enough.

faq: Is this gratitude journal app free?
Yes. It is completely free, with no subscription, no ads, no in-app purchases and no account. It is available on the App Store and Google Play.
Who can read my journal?
Your entries stay on your phone, and there is no account to sign in to. The journal is yours alone.
How much should I write each day?
A line or two is enough. What matters is noticing something real, not filling a page.
What is the difference between the journal and a gratitude meditation?
The journal is for writing, while the meditations are guided listening sessions. You can pair them: a short meditation first, then a few lines in the journal.
Does gratitude journaling work?

For many people, yes, in a modest way. In a 2003 study, Robert Emmons and Michael McCullough asked people to list what they were grateful for each week. They felt better about their lives than those who listed hassles. The benefits of gratitude journals vary from person to person, so see how it feels for you.
What are good gratitude journal prompts?
Try one of these gratitude prompts: What made me smile today? Who helped me, even a little? What did my body let me do? One prompt a day is plenty, and a single honest line counts.
What gratitude meditation benefits can I expect?

Many people say they notice more of what went well, and end the day on a softer note. Research on gratitude has looked mainly at writing, such as journals and letters, more than at meditation. So try a short session most evenings for a few weeks, then decide whether to keep it.

oracle.seo: The Oracle: Three Guided Meditations for How You Feel
oracle.desc: Type how you feel and the Oracle turns over three cards: three guided meditations for this moment, plus daily tips. Free, no ads, works offline.
oracle.h1: The MeditaDream Oracle: three meditations for how you feel
oracle.lead: Not sure which meditation to pick? Tell the Oracle how you feel, in your own words. It shuffles the deck and turns over three cards: three guided meditations chosen for this exact moment.

sections.h2: How does the Oracle work?
p: The screen asks one question: “How are you feeling?” You answer the way you would talk to a friend: “I feel anxious before a big meeting”, “I can’t sleep, my mind is racing”, “I feel lonely tonight”.
The Oracle replies with a sentence, written letter by letter, then three cards appear. Tap a card to see the meditation and its length, and start the session.
ul: “Surprise me” draws three meditations at random.
Ask again as many times as you like.
Everything happens on your phone: nothing you write is sent anywhere.

sections.h2: Examples: what the Oracle suggests
p: “I feel anxious before a big meeting”: “I can feel everything rushing. Here are three ways to slow down, right now.” Then When Everything Moves Too Fast (4 min), Finding Your Confidence Before a Challenge (4 min) and Breathing with the Whole Body (13 min).

“I can’t sleep, my mind is racing”: “Sleep comes more easily when you stop chasing it. Let yourself be carried.” Then Drifting into Sleep (16 min), Sleep Journey (27 min) and Body Asleep, Mind Awake (24 min).
“I want to explore the stars”: “Craving somewhere else? Close your eyes, the journey starts here.” Then The Unknown Planet (17 min) and two longer journeys through the galaxy and the northern lights.
Suggestions can change from one day to the next, so you keep discovering new sessions.

sections.h2: Daily tips that sound like you
p: Below the cards, the Oracle offers tips for the day. The more you use the app, the more personal they get: they draw on your journals, the reflections you note after sessions, your guides and your favorites, sometimes in your own words.
At first, when it barely knows you, it picks from nearly a hundred tips across fourteen themes: breath, sleep, gratitude, body awareness and more.

sections.h2: Why an oracle for meditation?
p: Often the hardest part is not meditating, it is choosing. Faced with so many sessions, you scroll, hesitate, then put the phone down. The Oracle turns that choice into one simple question and three answers.
It is not fortune-telling: the Oracle matches your words to meditations. Drawing cards is simply a gentle way to welcome whatever comes up.

faq: Is the Oracle free?
Yes, like the whole app: no subscription, no ads, no account.
Do I need an internet connection?
Not for the cards or the tips, which are worked out on your phone. You only need a connection to download a session the first time.
What happens to what I write?
It stays on your phone. Nothing is sent or shared.
Does the Oracle replace a professional?
No. It suggests wellbeing meditations. If you are going through a hard time, talk to someone close to you or to a professional.
How do I know which meditation is right for me?

Start from how you feel, not from a list. Tell the Oracle in your own words, and it suggests three meditations for this moment. You can also browse the 20 categories, or begin with a 4-minute session.

dragon.seo: Dragon Meditation Companion: A Pet That Grows With You
dragon.desc: Need meditation motivation? With dragon meditation, a companion hatches from an egg and grows with every minute you meditate. Eleven stages, free, no ads.
dragon.h1: Dragon meditation: a companion that grows as you practice
dragon.lead: In MeditaDream, dragon meditation is simple: every minute you meditate helps a companion grow. Your dragon hatches from an egg and moves to a new island as it matures. It flies across a sky that follows your clock and talks to you with a dry sense of humor.

sections.h2: How does dragon meditation work?
p: Your dragon grows with your total minutes of meditation, across eleven stages. The egg hatches after 10 minutes, the young dragon arrives after one hour of practice, the explorer at 300 minutes, the guardian at 1,000, and the cosmic dragon, the final stage, at 4,000 minutes.
ul: Dragon Egg: from the start
Hatchling Dragon: 10 minutes
Young Dragon: 60 minutes
Apprentice Dragon: 150 minutes
Adolescent Dragon: 225 minutes
Explorer Dragon: 300 minutes
Wayfarer Dragon: 500 minutes
Guardian Dragon: 1,000 minutes
Ancient Dragon: 2,000 minutes
Sage Dragon: 3,000 minutes
Cosmic Dragon: 4,000 minutes

sections.h2: Its island changes with it
p: Your dragon lives on an island floating in the sky, and the island evolves with it: a rock, a meadow, a sapling, a great tree, a waterfall, crystals, a temple, then a cosmic island.

It lands, moves around, meditates on the ground, then takes off for a flight. The sky follows your clock: daylight, sunset, a starry night with planets, an aurora on some nights, and visitors crossing the sky.

sections.h2: Its moods follow your meditation habit
p: Meditate three days in a row and it is happy; seven days and it gets excited; fourteen and it turns wise. If it does not see you for three days it gets bored, and after a week it feels lonely. It celebrates every new stage and every stamp in your passport.

It talks to you too. On your first meeting: “Hello. I’m your spiritual dragon. I was supposed to be a tiger. There was an administrative issue.” After thirty days: “Thirty days. I may need to revise my theories about humans.”

sections.h2: Accessories to unlock
p: As it grows, it earns items: a tiny lantern and a meditation cushion at the apprentice stage, an explorer’s hat, a compass and a passport bag at the explorer stage, a golden crown for the guardian, a halo for the sage, and a stardust cape for the cosmic dragon.

sections.h2: Why a dragon for meditation?
p: Because meditation consistency matters more than length, and it feeds on small joys. Watching your dragon hatch, then grow, makes you want to come back tomorrow, even for five minutes. That is meditation motivation in its simplest form. In Chinese tradition, the dragon also stands for strength and wisdom. Some people even adopt it as a dragon power animal.

faq: Does the dragon grow with short meditations?
Yes: it counts every minute, from 3-minute breaks to 40-minute journeys.
What happens if I stop for a few days?
It never shrinks and you lose nothing: it gets a little bored, then it is delighted when you come back.
Does the dragon cost anything?
No. MeditaDream is a daily meditation app, free, with no ads and no account, and the dragon comes with it.

journaux.seo: Dream Journal and 4 More Private Journals, Free
journaux.desc: A free dream journal, plus gratitude, emotion, signs and spiritual journals, all private and on your phone, inside a meditation app with no ads.
journaux.h1: A dream journal and four more: your private meditation journals
journaux.lead: MeditaDream does not stop when the session ends. Its dream journal and four other journals keep track of what you live through. They hold your dreams, your gratitude, your emotions, the signs you notice and your spiritual experiences. Each journal has its own sections, which work like guided journaling prompts. It is a simple way into mindful journaling, right next to your meditations.

sections.h2: Which journals are in the app?
ul: The dream journal, or dream diary, to write down your dreams on waking: places, characters, feelings and the ones that keep coming back.
The gratitude journal, to keep what did you good each day and what you take from it. Sections such as Emotional Growth work as journal prompts for self-growth. They also suit future self journaling.
The emotional journal, to name what you feel, look for why, and watch how it changes. On anxious evenings, try a few lines of journaling: anxiety often feels smaller once it is written down.
The signs journal, for the coincidences that strike you, what you made of them at the time, and later on.
The spiritual journal, to record your inner experiences and the insights they leave behind.

sections.h2: How to keep a dream journal
ol: Keep your phone by the bed and open the dream journal as soon as you wake, before getting up. This kind of morning journaling takes two minutes.
Write down what remains, even a fragment: an image, a place, a feeling. Do not try to tell the whole story.
Add a word about how the dream made you feel.
Read your notes back every week: recurring dreams and insistent symbols show up on their own. Over time, it becomes a personalized dream journal, and the first step toward lucid dreaming.

sections.h2: Your session history
p: Every meditation you finish goes into your history, with its date and length. You can note your reflections there, across eight themes, each with a short question. These meditation journal prompts, such as “What became clear or surprised you?”, make journaling for meditation easy. Read your notes later to see how far you have come.

sections.h2: Your writing stays yours
p: As a dream journal app, MeditaDream keeps everything on your phone, unlike a dream diary online. There is no account, no cloud, and nothing is sent. Every entry earns you a point, just like every meditation, which helps daily journaling become a habit. The Oracle also reads your journals right on your device, to offer tips that sound like you.

faq: Are the journals private?
Yes. They stay on your phone, with no account and nothing sent.
How much do the journals cost?
Nothing. MeditaDream is a free journaling app as much as a meditation app. The journals, with their free journal prompts, come with no subscription and no ads, like the meditations and the Oracle.
Can I keep a gratitude journal?
Yes, it is one of the five journals. The gratitude journal page explains how to keep it simple, with journaling ideas for every day.
What are good journal prompts for anxiety?

Keep them simple: What am I afraid of right now? What do I know for sure? What is one small thing I can do next? Write the answers in the emotional journal. If anxiety weighs on you, talk to a professional.
What are some daily journal prompts to start with?
Try these quick journal prompts, morning or evening: What did I notice today? What do I need right now? What am I looking forward to? Easy journal prompts like these take two minutes at most.
What are good journal prompts to get to know yourself?

Pick questions you can answer in a few lines: What gives me energy? What do I keep putting off, and why? What would I try if I could not fail? The Self Discovery section of the Gratitude & Growth journal is a good home for them.
Where do I start if I have never kept a journal?
Start with the sections: they act as beginner journal prompts, so you never face a blank page. Pick one journal, answer one section in a single line, and come back tomorrow.

creer.seo: Guided Meditation Script, Free: Write and Hear Your Own
creer.desc: Write a guided meditation script, free, and hear it read aloud on your phone, with your own pauses, even offline. No subscription, no ads.
creer.h1: My Meditations: write your own guided meditation script, free
creer.lead: Need a guided meditation script, free and made to measure? Write it yourself. In My Meditations, a line that helps you, a morning ritual or a visualization of your own becomes a session. The app reads it aloud, with the silences you choose.

sections.h2: How do you write your own guided meditation script?
ol: Give it a title, pick the reading language (English, French or Spanish) and a few keywords to sort it.
Write your script, one sentence per line. The preview shows how many sentences you have and the estimated length.
Add silences: a line “3 sec” on its own between two sentences, or [10] for ten seconds. An empty line also lets the script breathe.
Press play: a voice on your phone reads your meditation, even offline.

sections.h2: A guided meditation script, free to copy and make your own
p: Here is a short morning meditation, written the way the app expects, one sentence per line. Add a few more lines in the same spirit, and you have a 5-minute meditation script:
ul: Settle in, back straight, shoulders soft.
3 sec
Feel the cool air coming in through your nose.
And the warmer air going out.
5 sec
Set one simple intention for today.
When you are ready, gently open your eyes.

sections.h2: For a more natural voice
p: Playback uses the voices installed on your phone. The “enhanced” or “premium” voices sound far more natural: the app shows you how to download them, on iPhone and Android, and they then appear in the list. They matter most for slow scripts, such as a yoga nidra script or an NSDR script, where every pause counts.

sections.h2: Sort and find your meditations
p: Your meditations have a category of their own, sorted with keywords. Tag a chakra meditation script “energy” and a walking meditation script “morning”, or create your own keywords. They also help you find your texts in the library search. You can edit or delete them at any time. Listen to at least half of a session, and it counts in your history and your points.

faq: Do I need a connection to play my meditation?
No: playback happens on your phone, even in airplane mode.
Can I write in French or Spanish?
Yes: choose the language of each meditation and the voice follows.
Are my scripts shared?
No. They stay on your phone.
Can I write a loving kindness meditation script?

Yes. Write the classic metta phrases, one per line: May I be safe. May I be happy. May I live with ease. Then offer the same wishes to someone you love, with a silence after each. That is a simple metta meditation script.
How do I write a guided visualization meditation script?

Pick one calm place. For a beach guided imagery relaxation script, describe the sunset, the waves and the warm sand, sense by sense. Keep one image per line, and leave a few seconds of silence between them. Read it back once in the preview, then press play.
Is there a free 30-minute guided meditation script I can use?

The easiest one is the script you write yourself. Plan it in four parts: settling in, the breath, one long image, then the return. Write one sentence per line, and watch the estimated length in the preview until it reaches 30 minutes.

minuteur.seo: Meditation Timer: Free Silent Timer With Interval Bells
minuteur.desc: A free meditation timer app for silent meditation: 5 to 120 minutes, an interval bell every 1 to 10 minutes and a soft closing bell. No ads, offline.
minuteur.h1: Meditation timer: sit in silence, with a soft interval bell
minuteur.lead: The MeditaDream meditation timer is for the days you want silence instead of a voice. Choose a duration, pick an interval bell or none, and press Start. A large countdown fills the screen, and a soft chime tells you when it is over.

sections.h2: How does the meditation timer work?
p: Tap Timer on the home screen, then choose how long you want to sit: 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90 or 120 minutes.
Under “Chime every”, pick a bell every 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes, or “Off — only at the end”. Press Start: the countdown begins, and you can stop at any time.
ul: The bells still ring when your phone is locked.
It works offline: no account and no connection needed.
This meditation timer app is free, with no ads and no subscription.

sections.h2: A mindfulness bell app for silent meditation
p: In a meditation hall, a bell rings from time to time to bring everyone back to the present. The interval chime does the same on your phone.
Each chime is a single soft bowl, close to a Buddhist meditation bell sound. You hear it, you notice where your mind went, and you come back to the breath.
When you start, a bell every 2 minutes brings you back often. Later, a bell every 5 or 10 minutes leaves more room for silence.

sections.h2: Which timer settings for which goal?
p: The right settings depend on why you sit down. Here are three simple starting points.
ul: To learn to meditate: 5 or 10 minutes, with a bell every 2 minutes.
To reduce stress at work: 5 minutes, with only the closing bell.
For a long silent sitting, as in zen practice: 20 to 45 minutes, with a bell every 10 minutes.

sections.h2: Timed ambience: one sound, then silence
p: Timed ambience plays one ambient sound on its own, with no voice: woodland, after rain, ocean waves, a Chinese flute or a deep drone. For a Buddhist bell sound, pick Resonance, a singing bowl every four minutes.
Choose 5 minutes to 1 hour and set the volume. When the time is up, the sound fades out. It is a gentle way to fall asleep, or to read in calm.

sections.h2: A gentle meditation alarm
p: The Alarm reminds you to meditate at the time you choose, every day or only on the days you pick.
It is a soft notification, not a ringing alarm clock: a small invitation to take a few minutes for yourself.

sections.h2: Silent timer or guided meditation?
p: The timer suits you once you know what to do in silence: follow the breath, the body or the sounds around you.
If your mind wanders a lot, start with a guided session instead. The app has dozens of them, including short 4-minute meditations.

faq: Is the meditation timer free?
Yes. The timer, the alarm and timed ambience are free, like the whole app: no subscription, no ads, no account.
Does the timer work with the screen locked?
Yes. Start the timer, lock your phone and put it down: the interval bells and the closing bell still ring. Everything works offline.
Can I use it as a gong timer?
Yes, if you like a soft sound: the chime is a light bowl rather than a loud gong. It plays every 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes, and once at the end.
How long should a silent meditation last?
Start with 5 or 10 minutes a day. Add five minutes when the session starts to feel short. Sitting every day counts more than sitting long.
